findings.evidence: `if ml: ml.log_event("CONTRACT_CHECK", {...})` runs on every `main()` check. In scripts/master_ledger.py:181 the test-isolation guard only suppresses the write when `is_test_environment()` is true (MASTER_LEDGER_TEST=1 or PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST set) and no ledger_path or MASTER_LEDGER_PATH is given; otherwise the event is appended to the production ledger at DEFAULT_LEDGER (.claude/master_ledger.jsonl, master_ledger.py:34).
findings.suggested_investigation: Check the tests for agent_contract (e.g. tests that call main() or run the script via subprocess) and confirm they run under pytest or set MASTER_LEDGER_TEST=1/MASTER_LEDGER_PATH. Then run the test suite with those variables unset and diff .claude/master_ledger.jsonl before and after to see whether CONTRACT_CHECK lines are appended. Also check whether the `try: import master_ledger` at lines 29-32 resolves to scripts/master_ledger.py when agent_contract is imported from outside scripts/ (sys.path dependent).
findings.why_it_matters: Any test or tooling run that drives agent_contract.main() under a runner that does not set PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST or MASTER_LEDGER_TEST will write CONTRACT_CHECK records into the real ledger, polluting the audit trail that the gate/milestone tooling relies on. The new call is unconditional in agent_contract.py, so the isolation depends entirely on the environment of the caller.

notes: The added ledger hook is non-fatal: master_ledger.log_event never raises (master_ledger.py:161, 191-192), so it cannot change the exit code at line 324 or the PASS/FAIL verdict. The check verdict and return value (lines 305-324) are unchanged, so no gate was weakened. The `except ImportError` at lines 29-32 silently disables logging if the module is missing, which is a fragility rather than a gate weakening. Did not read any test files (not in the packet); the finding in f1 depends on how those tests invoke main(). No secret or credential paths were accessed. Tool calls used: 3 of 12.
